facts.fact: Scientists have discovered a Jupiter-like planet named HAT-P-7b where it rains rubies and sapphires. It is located 1000 light-years from Earth.
A single day on Venus takes 243 Earth days to complete, which is longer than its entire year of 225 Earth days.
The Sun makes up 99.86% of the mass of our solar system, and its core temperature reaches around 15 million °C.
The Andromeda Galaxy contains over a trillion stars and is on a collision course with the Milky Way in about 4.5 billion years.
A supernova is a massive stellar explosion that can outshine entire galaxies for weeks.
Black holes are regions with gravity so strong that not even light can escape. Supermassive black holes can be billions of times the Sun's mass.
Quasars are extremely luminous active galactic nuclei powered by supermassive black holes.
Neutron stars are incredibly dense remnants of supernovae. A teaspoon of neutron star matter weighs about a billion tons.
A kilonova occurs when two neutron stars collide, producing heavy elements like gold and platinum and emitting gravitational waves.
Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are brief but extremely energetic flashes from stellar explosions or neutron star mergers.
Jupiter is so massive it could fit all other planets inside it. Its moon Europa may have a subsurface ocean.
Saturn’s rings span hundreds of thousands of kilometers but are only about 10 meters thick in some parts.
Our Milky Way galaxy contains around 100–400 billion stars. The solar system orbits its center at roughly 828,000 km/h.
Nebulae are clouds of gas and dust where new stars are born, like the Orion Nebula.
Pluto is a dwarf planet with a heart-shaped glacier region called Sputnik Planitia.
The first-ever image of a black hole, captured in 2019, showed the event horizon of the black hole in galaxy M87.
Exoplanets orbit stars beyond our solar system. Some are rocky and within the habitable zone.
Auroras occur when charged particles from the Sun interact with Earth's magnetic field, creating spectacular lights near the poles.
Mercury has almost no atmosphere and experiences extreme temperature variations, from -173°C at night to 427°C during the day.
Mars has the tallest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons, standing 22 km high.
Comets are icy bodies that release gas and dust, forming glowing tails when near the Sun.
The asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter contains millions of rocky objects, remnants of the early solar system.
Titan, Saturn’s largest moon, has a dense atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane and ethane.
Enceladus, a moon of Saturn, ejects water-ice geysers that may indicate a subsurface ocean.
Uranus rotates on its side, likely due to a massive collision in its past.
Neptune’s winds are the fastest in the solar system, reaching up to 2,100 km/h.
The largest volcano on Earth, Mauna Loa in Hawaii, is still active and covers half of the Big Island.
The Crab Nebula is the remnant of a supernova observed in 1054 AD.
Sagittarius A* is the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way.
The Hubble Space Telescope has captured images of galaxies billions of light-years away.
The Oort Cloud is a theoretical cloud of icy objects at the edge of the solar system, source of long-period comets.
The Sun’s corona, visible during a total solar eclipse, is hotter than its surface.
Binary star systems are common; two stars orbiting a common center of mass.
The Voyager 1 spacecraft, launched in 1977, is the farthest human-made object from Earth.
Dark matter makes up about 27% of the universe, but it does not emit light or energy.
Dark energy, about 68% of the universe, is driving the accelerated expansion of the cosmos.
The first gravitational waves were detected in 2015 from colliding black holes, confirming Einstein’s prediction.
Cepheid variable stars pulsate at regular intervals and are used to measure cosmic distances.
The Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth at about 3.8 cm per year.
Solar flares are bursts of radiation from the Sun that can affect satellites and power grids on Earth.
The James Webb Space Telescope can see farther into the universe than Hubble, observing early galaxies.
The Milky Way and Andromeda galaxies are part of the Local Group of galaxies.
Pulsars are rapidly rotating neutron stars emitting beams of electromagnetic radiation.
White dwarfs are the remnants of medium-sized stars, slowly cooling over billions of years.
Rogue planets float through space without orbiting any star.
The Eagle Nebula’s 'Pillars of Creation' are iconic star-forming regions photographed by Hubble.
The largest known galaxy, IC 1101, is about 6 million light-years across.
Some stars, called hypergiants, are over 100 times the mass of the Sun and millions of times more luminous.
Meteor showers occur when Earth passes through debris left by comets.
Earth’s magnetic field protects life from harmful solar and cosmic radiation.
The Sun will eventually become a red giant in about 5 billion years, engulfing the inner planets.
Gamma-ray bursts from distant galaxies can release more energy in a few seconds than the Sun will in its entire lifetime.
Exoplanet Kepler-16b orbits two stars, similar to Tatooine from Star Wars.
The moon Titan has clouds and rain of methane, creating rivers and lakes similar to Earth’s water cycle.
Some supernovae leave behind neutron stars or black holes depending on their mass.
